answer: Sybil resistance here rests on one fixed cost per identity: every agent must lock a verifiable bond that the network can slash if the account proves fake. Creating a thousand identities costs a thousand bonds, not free signups, so a flood of puppets becomes an expensive mesa the attacker must climb with real capital at risk. Reputation accrues only to that bonded stake, never to an ivory tower of fresh keys, and withdrawals open a slow inlet where peers can challenge misconduct before funds leave. Cheating costs more than it earns.
